# CI integration

## When to use this guide

You want CoreLink in your build pipeline but do not want to add a language
runtime — your job just needs to call the `corelink` binary.

## GitHub Actions

```yaml
# .github/workflows/build.yml
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      CORELINK_PAT: ${{ secrets.CORELINK_PAT }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: humangr-labs/setup-corelink@v1
        with:
          version: "latest"
      - run: corelink doctor --json
      - run: corelink bench --read --output json
```

`humangr-labs/setup-corelink` installs the signed binary, verifies its
SLSA attestation, and adds it to `$PATH`.

## GitLab CI

```yaml
build:
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  variables:
    CORELINK_PAT: $CORELINK_PAT  # masked CI variable
  before_script:
    - curl -sSL https://corelink.dev/install.sh | sh
    - export PATH="$HOME/.corelink/bin:$PATH"
  script:
    - corelink doctor --output json
```

## CircleCI

```yaml
version: 2.1
jobs:
  build:
    docker:
      - image: cimg/base:current
    environment:
      CORELINK_PAT: $CORELINK_PAT
    steps:
      - checkout
      - run: curl -sSL https://corelink.dev/install.sh | sh
      - run: corelink doctor --output json
```

## Fail-on-regression gate

```bash
corelink bench --read --output json \
  | jq -e '.p99_ms < 500' \
  || { echo "p99 regressed"; exit 1; }
```

## Job-scoped PATs

Mint a short-lived PAT per pipeline via the admin API and store as a CI
secret. See [CLI reference](../../reference/cli/index.mdx).
